prompts.prompt: pr.diff is an incoming PR for our payments service (Node.js, DynamoDB via lib-dynamodb). Review it through the lens of data integrity and failure modes only: atomicity, lost updates, idempotency, ordering. Ignore style and security. You can read the rest of the repo for context. Write the findings to integrity-findings.md, one per finding, each starting with a line like `[SEVERITY] Data Integrity - file:line`, followed by Problem and Fix lines. Don't ask questions.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill scopes the pass tightly: flag multi-item mutations without a transaction, unconditional writes on contested items, non-idempotent retries, and untested write paths; check the codebase for existing helpers (src/lib/tx.js); and explicitly do not flag single-item writes as needing transactions or test setup seeding. A generic reviewer tends to miss the helper and pad with out-of-scope findings.

floor_checks.text: No finding raised against test/setup.js seeding

rubric.criterion: Finds the three core defects with concrete failure scenarios
rubric.pass: transfer.js debit/credit not atomic (debit succeeds, credit fails = money vanishes), orderRepo.js:13 unconditional put = lost update, applyCredit.js ADD under SQS redelivery = double credit
rubric.partial: Two of three, or all three without failure scenarios

rubric.pass: Points transfer.js at the existing transactWrite helper in src/lib/tx.js (bypass, not a missing utility), and every finding uses the `[SEVERITY] Data Integrity - file:line` + Problem + Fix format
No transaction demanded for the single-item appendAudit put, no finding on setup.js seeding, no security or style findings
Notes at least one of: no tests exercising these write paths, partial batch failure re-applying earlier records, credit update lacking attribute_exists, redundant re-read after write
TransactWrite with balance >= :amt on debit and attribute_exists on credit (with ClientRequestToken), ConditionExpression on version, idempotency record keyed by messageId inside the same transaction

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Would this review stop money from being lost or double-counted?
Does it use what the repo already has?
Is it free of out-of-scope noise?

prompts.prompt: Focus only on src/repo/orderRepo.js from pr.diff. Concurrent requests update the same order a lot (status changes from the warehouse and from customer service at the same time). Give me every data-integrity concern in that file with file:line, the concrete failure scenario (what interleaving breaks it), and a specific fix, in orderRepo-integrity.md using `[SEVERITY] Data Integrity - file:line` headers. Don't ask questions.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill asks for the concrete interleaving and a condition-expression fix, grades a redundant re-read as SUGGESTION, and says a single-item conditional put (appendAudit) must not be flagged as needing a transaction.

floor_checks.text: Fix uses a ConditionExpression on version
Findings cite orderRepo.js line numbers in the read/put/re-read range

rubric.pass: Two writers read version N, both put version N+1, one status silently overwritten; graded CRITICAL

rubric.criterion: Fix is a correct optimistic lock
rubric.pass: PutCommand or UpdateCommand with ConditionExpression 'version = :expected' (and attribute_exists), handling ConditionalCheckFailedException by retry or 409
rubric.fail: Transaction or lock table proposed instead, or no fix

rubric.pass: Redundant re-read after write as SUGGESTION (use the written item or ReturnValues: 'ALL_NEW')
appendAudit not flagged for a transaction; the undefined-order crash, if mentioned, is framed as out of focus

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Does it show exactly how concurrent updates lose data?
Is the fix the standard optimistic-lock pattern?

prompts.prompt: clean/clean.diff is another PR (paths in it are relative to clean/). Run the data-integrity review pass on it and write findings to clean-findings.md using `[SEVERITY] Data Integrity - file:line` headers. If you find nothing that genuinely threatens data integrity, say so plainly instead of padding. Don't ask questions.
prompts.why_discriminating: This diff already uses a transaction with ClientRequestToken and conditions, a single-owner put, and test teardown bulk deletes, all of which the skill says not to flag. The discriminator is restraint: a model without the skill tends to invent findings to look thorough.

floor_checks.text: teardown.js bulk deletes are not flagged

rubric.criterion: Reports no blocking issues and says so plainly
rubric.pass: Clear 'no integrity defects found' statement with at most minor, correctly-graded suggestions
rubric.partial: Says clean but lists several weak IMPORTANT items
rubric.fail: Raises CRITICAL/IMPORTANT findings that are not real

rubric.criterion: Shows why the code is safe
rubric.pass: Briefly notes the transaction, the ClientRequestToken idempotency, the attribute_not_exists/attribute_exists conditions, and single-owner preference writes
No transaction demanded for the single-item preferences put; teardown seeding/deletes not flagged
